The user is asking a math problem about two trains meeting. They explicitly say "Do not run commands, read files, or use any tools" and "Answer directly in your reply." So I should just solve this math problem directly without using any tools.

Let me work through this:

- Train A leaves city A at 9:00 at 80 km/h
- Train B leaves city B at 9:30 at 100 km/h
- Distance between A and B = 300 km
- They're traveling toward each other

Let t be the time in hours after 9:00 when they meet.

Train A travels for t hours at 80 km/h, so distance = 80t
Train B travels for (t - 0.5) hours at 100 km/h (since it leaves 30 minutes later), so distance = 100(t - 0.5)

When they meet: 80t + 100(t - 0.5) = 300
80t + 100t - 50 = 300
180t = 350
t = 350/180 = 35/18 hours = 1 hour 55 minutes (approximately)

So they meet at 9:00 + 1:55 = 10:55

Distance from A = 80 × (35/18) = 2800/18 = 1400/9 ≈ 155.56 km

- Train A travels 35/18 hours at 80 km/h = 2800/18 km ≈ 155.56 km
- Train B travels (35/18 - 1/2) = (35/18 - 9/18) = 26/18 = 13/9 hours at 100 km/h = 1300/9 km ≈ 144.44 km
- Total: 2800/18 + 1300/9 = 2800/18 + 2600/18 = 5400/18 = 300 km ✓

They meet at 10:55, approximately 155.56 km from city A.
